steps.text: Three things go wrong at narrow widths, and they are all the same bug: the header lays out as if every chip were optional. I'll start with the label helper, because the truncation rule is what the spacing has to be measured against.
Nothing owns truncation - three surfaces each cut the string their own way, which is why the card title and the board tile disagree about the same session.
Five tests, green. The helper is in; the spacing pass is next and it needs one decision from you first.

todos.content: One truncation helper the card, tile and rail all use
Even the chip spacing in the card header
Keep the focus ring visible on the chips that became buttons

steps.text: The header currently sets no gap and leans on each chip's own padding, so the glyph chips sit tighter than the text ones. Evening it out changes every card's header, so I want your call on the rule rather than picking one.

questions.question: How should the header space its chips?

options.label: One 6px gap on the row
options.description: the row owns the spacing and every chip drops its own margins - consistent, and it re-flows correctly when a chip is absent

options.label: Keep per-chip margins
options.description: a smaller diff today, but the row still reads unevenly the moment a chip is conditional

questions.question: What should a glyph-only chip do about its accessible name?

options.label: Keep the glyph and add a label
options.description: the glyph stays decorative and the control carries a real name - two characters wider, readable by everything

options.label: Glyph with a tooltip only
options.description: narrowest, but the accessible name is then whatever the tooltip happens to say
